html:
SMTO-CMP-0013 — Some of the proof that the task is done is incomplete

GUID: ee9974e8-4021-4401-8a5f-c62e9cfed769
Slug: completion-incomplete-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI model pointed to results that are incomplete, didn't actually run, or came from a different kind of step than it claimed. SMTO won't call the task done on that basis. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task's steps for any that failed, stopped early, were cut short or didn't run. Those are the results SMTO couldn't use to prove the task is done.
  2. Check the real result of those steps yourself, for example in the file, system or service involved. The work may be done even though its saved result is incomplete.
  3. Select Resume, or tell SMTO which parts you confirmed in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task and select Continue. SMTO can then read the missing details or finish only what's left, without repeating finished work.
  4. If you've confirmed the work yourself, you can turn off "Enforce this check for this run" on the check card under the task. SMTO then rechecks its saved answer for this task only, without running anything again.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply matches what you checked yourself.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't select Restart task while that is unclear; it could repeat changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • With completeness checks enabled, a cited receipt or result was incomplete, unexecuted, or did not match the expected capability during completion assessment (reason incomplete_evidence).

What this means

  • Enabled completeness checks find a receipt/result incomplete, unexecuted or mismatched to the expected capability during completion assessment. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Enabled completeness checks find a receipt/result incomplete, unexecuted or mismatched to the expected capability during completion assessment.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect receipt complete/executed/capability fields and exact operation correlation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect complete, executed and capability_id on the cited receipt and its result-index entry (resolve_evidence and validate_completion in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py; attempt_direct_completion in native/direct_completion.py). Read the remaining bounded observation or the correctly correlated receipt in this run before declaring completion; the completion.complete_observation Agent Check controls enforcement.
  • Obtain the remaining observation or receipt fields before making a complete claim.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation has complete eligible correlated evidence before a complete claim is accepted.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
